adults.title: Courage and Charity, Together
adults.big_idea: Disciples of Jesus Christ stand for truth and show love at the same time, and the Lord will help us do both.
adults.objective: Learners will identify whether they most need greater conviction or greater charity and choose one of Elder Gilbert's five principles to practice in a real relationship this week.
prepare: Read Elder Clark G. Gilbert's talk, Teach Truth with Love, and mark the five principles.
Write TRUTH and LOVE on the board as two column headings, with space between them.
Bring paper and pens for silent writing.
Ask learners to open the talk on their phones or bring a few printed copies for groups.
Pray to know who in your class is carrying a strained relationship, and teach with them in mind.

segments.name: Which is harder for you?
steps: Begin with prayer. Then describe a generic situation: at a family dinner, a relative you love speaks sharply against something you hold sacred. Everyone looks at you.
Point to the two headings on the board. Ask the first question below and let two or three people answer briefly.
Read the first key quote (T36.01) aloud. Explain that Elder Gilbert, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, amplified five principles that President Oaks once taught for standing for truth with love.
questions: In a moment like that, which comes less naturally to you: speaking up for what is true, or staying loving while you do?

segments.name: Look inward first
steps: Tell how Elder Gilbert said that when President Nelson spoke on peacemaking, he started a mental list of everyone he thought needed the message. President Nelson then cautioned listeners to look into their own hearts.
Read the invitation from T36.02 (see invitations). Point out that Elder Gilbert extended it to all of us.
Hand out paper. Give one quiet minute for each person to write the name or initials of one relationship where truth and love feel hard to hold together. No one will be asked to share it.

segments.name: Five principles in small groups
steps: Divide into five groups (or pairs) and give each one principle from the talk: 1. Avoid overly contentious settings. 2. Find common ground. 3. Be a light. 4. Hold to truth even in our outreach. 5. Stay anchored in Jesus Christ.
Ask each group to read that section of the talk and prepare a one-minute report answering the two questions below. Allow five minutes.
Hear the five reports, one minute each. As groups report, write a short phrase for each principle on the board between TRUTH and LOVE.

When principle 1 is reported, add Elder Andersen's words (see aligned quotes). When principle 2 is reported, make sure the class hears that Elder Gilbert listened for nearly two hours before he invited.
questions: What did Elder Gilbert teach or tell in this section that stays with you?
Where could this principle change an ordinary conversation at home, at work, or online?

segments.name: How the Savior held both
steps: Read John 8:1–11 together, with learners following in their own scriptures. Ask them to look for what the Savior did that showed love and what He said that held to truth.
Read President Holland's words that Elder Gilbert quoted (see aligned quotes).
Read the key quote from T36.17 about minimizing God's laws. Discuss the questions below. Let learners carry the conversation; add little.
questions: What do you learn about the Savior from the way He treated this woman?
When has someone told you a hard truth in a way that left you sure you were loved? What did that person do?

segments.name: A charity check
steps: Explain that for the fifth principle Elder Gilbert asked us to check ourselves against the attributes of charity.
Invite everyone to read Moroni 7:45 silently with the relationship they wrote down in mind, and to mark one phrase they do well and one phrase they want the Lord's help with.

Ask one or two volunteers to share the phrase they chose and why. This is your check for understanding: listen for whether learners connect charity with standing for truth, not with staying silent about it.
questions: Which phrase in this verse would most change the way you speak up for truth?

segments.name: Choose and act
steps: Read the key quote from T36.20. Point out Elder Gilbert's observation that for some this will require greater conviction and for others greater charity.
Ask each person to write under the name on their paper: which one do I need more of, and which of the five principles will I practice with this person this week?
Share Elder Gilbert's promise: he knows the Lord will help us as we strive to teach truth with love. Bear your own brief testimony of the Savior.
Tell the class you will begin next week by asking for one or two experiences of listening longer, staying quiet with dignity, or speaking a truth more kindly.

key_quotes.text: It takes courage to stand for truth. It takes even more courage to stand for truth with love.
I may have won the debate in the moment, but I lost the Spirit and I failed to help my struggling friend.
When we try to love others by minimizing God’s laws, we separate ourselves from the one person who loves them the very most.
For disciples of Jesus Christ, truth and love always walk together.

scriptures.use: Read together in the fourth segment. Look for what the Savior did that showed love and what He said that held to truth; Elder Gilbert cites verse 11.
Read silently in the fifth segment as a personal check. Mark one attribute of charity you do well and one you want the Lord's help with.
Optional: read when the group reports on finding common ground, and ask how being loved first makes a person ready to hear truth.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Jeffrey R. Holland
aligned_quotes.text: As near as I can tell, Christ never once withheld His love from anyone, but He also never once said to anyone, ‘Because I love you, you are exempt from keeping my commandments.’

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Neil L. Andersen
aligned_quotes.text: There are times when being a peacemaker means that we resist the impulse to respond and instead, with dignity, remain quiet.

invitations.text: I also hope that you will look deeply into your [own] heart to see if there are shards of pride or jealousy that prevent you from becoming a peacemaker.” I extend that same invitation to all of us today.

takeaways: Truth and love are not rivals; in Jesus Christ they always walk together.
Listening first and living my covenants often open more doors than an argument.
The Lord will help me as I strive to teach truth with love.
act: Before a conversation you expect to be tense, pray by name for the person and ask what he or she may be carrying that you cannot see.
In one conversation this week, listen without interrupting until the other person has finished, then find one thing you truly agree on before you say anything else.
Read Moroni 7:45 each morning this week and choose one attribute to practice that day.
If you have spoken a truth harshly to someone, go back and apologize for the way you said it, without withdrawing the truth.
adapt: At home or in a very small group: skip the groups. Read the five principle headings aloud, let each person choose the one that speaks to them, and read that section together.
In a large class: form groups by rows and assign the five principles more than once; hear one report per principle.
If time is short: keep the silent writing, the John 8 discussion, and the closing choice. Summarize the five principles from the board in one minute.

youth.title: Keep the Friend, Keep the Truth
youth.big_idea: Following Jesus Christ means standing for what is true and loving people at the same time, and He will help us do both.
youth.objective: Youth will practice answering a hard comment about their beliefs in a way that is both true and loving, and choose one of Elder Gilbert's five principles to try with a real person this week.
prepare: Read Elder Clark G. Gilbert's talk, Teach Truth with Love, especially the story of his friend and the five principles.
Write the five principles on the board: 1. Avoid overly contentious settings. 2. Find common ground. 3. Be a light. 4. Hold to truth even in our outreach. 5. Stay anchored in Jesus Christ.
Write the four scenarios from the third segment on four slips of paper.
Bring paper and pens. Ask youth to have scriptures or phones ready for John 8 and Moroni 7.

segments.name: Pick a wall
steps: After an opening prayer, have everyone stand. Say: Move to the left wall if it is harder for you to speak up for what you believe. Move to the right wall if it is harder for you to stay kind when someone attacks what you believe.
Ask one person from each wall to say why in a sentence.
Have them sit. Read the first key quote (T36.01) and explain that Elder Gilbert, of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles, taught that disciples need both.

segments.name: The debate he won
steps: Tell the story in Elder Gilbert's talk: he had a friend who had once been spiritually faithful but was now attacking the Church. Elder Gilbert was frustrated because he knew his friend knew better. Instead of considering that his friend might be hurting for reasons he could not see, he shot back an angry reply.
Ask a youth to read the key quote from T36.08 aloud.
Discuss the questions below in pairs for one minute, then hear two or three answers.
questions: Elder Gilbert said he stood for truth that day. What was missing, and what did it cost?
What does it look like online or at school to win the argument and lose the friend?

segments.name: True and loving: the reply challenge
steps: Point to the five principles on the board and give a ten-second summary of each from the talk. For principle 2, mention that Elder Gilbert once listened to people's concerns for nearly two hours before he invited them to stake conference, and each one accepted.

Form four teams and give each a scenario slip: (a) In a group chat, someone mocks people who believe in God. (b) A friend who has stopped coming to church tells you none of it is real. (c) A friend says that if you really cared about people you would drop your standards. (d) A classmate keeps pushing you to argue about religion in front of others.

Give teams three minutes to plan a response that is both true and loving, using at least one of the five principles. Remind them that sometimes the best response is to listen, or to say nothing for now.

Each team shares its response in under a minute. The rest of the class names which principle they heard and holds up one to five fingers twice: once for how true it was, once for how loving. The goal is high on both.
This is your check for understanding: if a response drops the truth to keep the peace, or drops kindness to make the point, ask the class how to bring the missing half back.

segments.name: What Jesus did
steps: Read John 8:1–11 together, a few verses each. Ask half the class to watch for how the Savior showed love and the other half to watch for how He held to truth.
Hear what each half found. Then read President Holland's words that Elder Gilbert quoted (see aligned quotes).
Read the key quote from T36.11 about keeping covenants. Ask the questions below.
questions: Why do you think the Savior did both, instead of choosing one?
Who in your life tells you the truth and you still know that person loves you? How do they do it?

segments.name: Look in the mirror
steps: Explain that Elder Gilbert worried some listeners would see only other people's shortcomings and forget their own. Read the invitation from T36.02 (see invitations). Make clear that the words are President Nelson's, from his talk on peacemaking, and that Elder Gilbert extended the same invitation to all of us.
Have youth open Moroni 7:45 on their phones or in their scriptures and read it silently. Elder Gilbert asked us to check ourselves against this list when we stand for truth.
On paper, each youth writes one phrase from the verse to work on and the first name or initials of one person they want to treat that way. Papers stay private.

segments.name: This week
steps: Read the key quote from T36.20. Point out that Elder Gilbert said some of us will need greater conviction and others greater charity.
Invite each youth to choose one item from the act list, or write their own, and to tell a partner what they chose.
Share Elder Gilbert's promise that the Lord will help us as we strive to teach truth with love, and add your own testimony of the Savior.
Tell them you will open next week by asking who tried it and what happened.

key_quotes.text: It takes courage to stand for truth. It takes even more courage to stand for truth with love.
I may have won the debate in the moment, but I lost the Spirit and I failed to help my struggling friend.
The best way to help someone else keep their covenants is to keep your covenants.
For disciples of Jesus Christ, truth and love always walk together.

scriptures.use: Read aloud in the fourth segment. Half the class looks for how the Savior showed love; half looks for how He held to truth. Elder Gilbert cites verse 11.
Read silently in the fifth segment. Each youth picks one phrase about charity to work on with a specific person.
Optional: read during the reply challenge when you describe principle 2, and ask why people listen better to someone who loved them first.

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Jeffrey R. Holland
aligned_quotes.text: As near as I can tell, Christ never once withheld His love from anyone, but He also never once said to anyone, ‘Because I love you, you are exempt from keeping my commandments.’

aligned_quotes.speaker: President Russell M. Nelson
aligned_quotes.text: Let your skeptical friends see how much you love the Lord and His gospel. Surprise their doubting hearts with your believing heart!

invitations.text: I also hope that you will look deeply into your [own] heart to see if there are shards of pride or jealousy that prevent you from becoming a peacemaker.” I extend that same invitation to all of us today.

takeaways: I do not have to choose between truth and love; Jesus Christ never did.
Winning an argument is not the same as helping a friend.
The Lord will help me as I try to share truth with love.
act: The next time a comment about your beliefs makes you angry, wait before you answer. Pray first, and decide whether to reply, to listen, or to stay quiet for now.
Ask a friend who sees things differently to tell you what they think and why. Listen all the way through and find one thing you agree on.
Choose one standard you will keep quietly and cheerfully this week, so that your example is the light.
Read Moroni 7:45 once a day and work on the phrase you wrote down.
adapt: At home or with two or three youth: do the reply challenge together, taking one scenario at a time and building the response as a group.
In a large class: make more teams and reuse the scenarios; have only four teams share and the others rate.
If time is short: keep the story of Elder Gilbert's friend, two scenarios, and the closing choice for the week.

children.title: Truth and Love Walk Together
children.big_idea: I can say what is true in a kind way, like Jesus.
children.objective: Children will be able to say the lesson's truth in their own words and show one way to say something true with a kind voice.
prepare: Read Elder Clark G. Gilbert's talk, Teach Truth with Love, especially the story of the visit where he listened first.
Bring a flashlight, paper, and crayons.
Clear a space where children can hop and walk safely.
Be ready to sing Jesus Said Love Everyone.

segments.name: Welcome and song
steps: Greet each child by name and invite a child to pray.
Sing Jesus Said Love Everyone together, with simple actions.
Say: Today we will learn that I can say what is true in a kind way, like Jesus. Have the children repeat it with you once.

segments.name: Two feet
steps: Have the children stand with room around them. Say: This foot is TRUTH. Hop on it carefully to the other side of the room. Is hopping easy or wobbly?
Say: This other foot is LOVE. Hop back on only that foot. Still wobbly.
Now walk across on both feet. Say: Elder Gilbert, an Apostle of Jesus Christ, taught that truth and love always walk together. We need both feet.
Have the children march in place and say with each step: truth, love, truth, love.

segments.name: The story of listening first
steps: Seat the children and tell the story simply: Elder Gilbert went with a stake president to visit a home. When they arrived, five people were waiting inside, and each one had a different worry.

Continue: Elder Gilbert asked where they wanted to start. He wanted to speak up, but the Spirit kept prompting him to wait. So he listened and listened, for nearly two hours. He began to understand them. Then he invited them to come to stake conference that evening, and every one of them said yes.

Act it out. Choose one child to be the visitor and up to five to be the people in the home. The visitor cups a hand behind an ear and listens while each person says, I have a worry. Then the visitor says, Will you come to church with me? and they all answer, Yes.
Repeat with new children so more have a turn. Ask the questions below.
questions: What did Elder Gilbert do first?
How do you feel when someone really listens to you?

segments.name: Kind voice or grumpy voice
steps: Explain that the same true words can be said in a kind way or an unkind way. Children stand up tall if they hear a kind voice and crouch down small if they hear a grumpy voice.
Say each of these true sentences twice, once grumpy and once kind, in mixed order: It is time to clean up. Please do not push. That is not how the game goes. I want to choose the right.
Let the children take turns saying one of the sentences in a kind voice while the others stand up tall.
Share Elder Kyungu's words from this conference (see aligned quotes) in simple terms: we use words that help people understand and feel peace.

segments.name: Be a light
steps: Dim the lights if you can and turn on the flashlight. Ask: Does the flashlight have to shout to help us see? It simply shines.
Say: Elder Gilbert taught us to be a light. When we love Jesus and choose the right, other people can see it.

Pass the flashlight around the circle. Each child holding it finishes this sentence: I can be a light when I ... Help younger children with ideas such as pray, share, tell the truth, or help a friend.

segments.name: Draw it
steps: Give each child paper and crayons. Invite them to draw themselves saying something true in a kind way to a friend or someone at home.
As they draw, move from child to child and ask: What are you saying in your picture? How are you being kind? This is your check for understanding.
Help each child write or dictate the words at the top: Truth and love walk together.

segments.name: Remember and do
steps: Have the children hold up their pictures and say together: I can say what is true in a kind way, like Jesus.
Tell them Elder Gilbert said he knows the Lord will help us as we strive to teach truth with love. Testify that Jesus loves them and will help them.
Invite each child to choose one thing to do this week: listen first, or use a kind voice. Ask them to take their picture home and tell someone about it.
Tell them that next week you will ask who listened first or used a kind voice, and close with prayer.

key_quotes.text: For disciples of Jesus Christ, truth and love always walk together.
I know the Lord will help us as we strive to teach truth with love.

scriptures.use: After the listening story, have an older child read it aloud. Ask: Who loved us first? How can we love others first, as Elder Gilbert did by listening?
During the kind voice game, have an older child read the first line and listen for the word kind. Younger children repeat the word together.

aligned_quotes.speaker: Elder Kyungu
aligned_quotes.text: let us use words that encourage understanding and peace

takeaways: I can listen first and use a kind voice.
Jesus will help me say what is true with love.
act: When someone is talking to you this week, listen all the way to the end before you answer.
Say one true thing in a kind voice each day, such as asking for a turn or reminding someone of a rule.
Be a light by doing one thing that shows you love Jesus, and tell your family about it.

adapt.younger: For ages 3–7: keep the story to four or five sentences and act it out twice. Spend extra time on hopping and marching, and repeat the words truth and love walk together after every activity. Let helpers hold the flashlight with the youngest children and write the words on their drawings.
adapt.older: For ages 8–11: have them read 1 John 4:19 and Moroni 7:45 aloud and lead the kind voice game by making up their own true sentences. Ask a harder question: When is it hard to be kind and truthful at the same time, and what could you do? Let one of them retell the listening story for the younger children.
